MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 18, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:01 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina,  Pope,  Ciarolla,  Johnson,
  Holdsworth, Bain, and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  5.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PILOT PROGRAM FOR ALL-DAY TENNIS CLUB COURT RESERVATIONS AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Pilot Program for all-day tennis
  club reservations at Ernie Howlett Park (as per the agenda materials).

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the tennis pro was in favor of the pilot program, in
  response to COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas clarified the current
  tennis club membership policies regarding the use of the courts by members and
  non-members. She also noted that since staff is not currently present during the
  afternoon hours Monday-Friday, therefore the use between members and non-
  members is unknown during those hours.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
March 18, 2025
   Supervisor Pinuelas stated that during the pilot program, reservation fees would
  be charged during all hours of operation. She also stated that it is difficult holding
  participants to current court policies due to not having staff present during the
  current free use play on weekday afternoons, in response to CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that pickleball
  groups could have a tennis club member from their group, reserve a court for their
  use. She also noted that the department open-play program will still be held on
  Fridays during the pilot program continuing to allow free play during that time.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA inquired if there is a no-show policy regarding reservations.
  Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that there currently is a no-show policy and that a
  court will be released if the reserved party does not arrive after a certain amount
  of time.

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  RECOMMEND TO CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE PROPOSED SIX-
  MONTH PILOT PROGRAM FOR ALL DAY TENNIS CLUB
  RESERVATIONS AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  6.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  RECREATION REGISTRATION SYSTEM

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the new recreation registration
  system including a preview of the system (as per the agenda materials).

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked if Apple Pay or Pay Pal were a payment option with the
  registration system. Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that Apple Pay is currently a
  payment option.

  In response to VICE CHAIR POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff will
  continue to use the software for point-of-sale purchases at the City Celebration
  event and will look into using the software for pre-event wristband sales.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if instructors of City sponsored programs would
  have to the software. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that instructors will have limited
  access to the software to review rosters and other small aspects of their programs.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
March 18, 2025
   Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would confirm the main account holder’s
  ability to sign off on waivers for spouses or participants under the age of 18 if they
  are not the legal parent or guardian, in response to COMMISSIONER JOHNSON.

  B.  DOG RUN FEASIBILITY (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update on the feasibility study for establishing a
  dog park or dog run in the city. She reported that Staff had evaluated potential
  spaces but found challenges such as inadequate space, parking limitations,
  proximity to homes, site preparation needs, and accessibility concerns. The City
  Council agreed with the interest in having a dog run or park but is not planning to
  budget for further research during the next budget cycle due to other ongoing
  projects. She stated the item will remain on the future projects list for future
  consideration.

  C.  FEE STUDY UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  ACM Davis provided an update on the fee study for Community Services. She
  explained that while the COMMISSION reviews fees annually based on cost-of-
  living increases, a formal analysis of the fee structure has not been done in
  recent history. The City plans to engage a consultant to analyze the City's costs,
  including staffing, maintenance, water, and facility wear and tear, to achieve cost
  recovery while also considering comparable markets for recreation programs and
  services.

  D.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update regarding the upcoming Mayor’s
  Breakfast Ride Event. She mentioned that the event will take place on Saturday,
  May 10 and that Staff is excited to have the Scouts back for their annual pancake
  breakfast. She also noted that invitations will be sent to the Commissioners in the
  upcoming weeks.

  E.  HILLS ARE ALIVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update on the upcoming Hills Are Alive 5k/10k
  Race. She updated the Commission about registration, sponsorships and
  ongoing marketing efforts.

  F.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reminded Commissioners that their Form 700 forms are due
  by April 1st and offered to collect any completed forms at the end of the meeting.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
March 18, 2025
   7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired about the Pedro Pet Pals pet adoption event and
  if there was any update. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that as of right now they
  informed Staff that there is no urgent need for an event, but they are appreciative
  of the opportunity to hold an event when necessary.

  COMMISSIONER POPE inquired if there was an update regarding the possibility
  of a banner program for veterans and active military service members. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that Staff is hoping to connect with other cities, research possible
  banner locations and is hoping to report something back to the Commission soon.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if Staff have considered partnering with a
  local non-profit organization during the Hills Are Alive event where some of the
  registration revenue could be donated to the organization based on their
  assistance and participation during the event. ACM Davis stated that historically
  the City has not donated funds raised during Pepper Tree fundraising events to
  non-profit organizations, but this could be brought to the attention of the event
  subcommittee prior to next year’s event.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for an update regarding the Nature Center project.
  ACM Davis provided a brief update regarding the current process of the Nature
  Center project including that the plans and permits are approved but the initial bids
  were rejected by City Council. She noted that there are some alternatives to assist
  in receiving more palatable bid results that better match budgeted funds as well as
  looking at alternatives to secure additional funds through grants and donors to help
  bridge the funding gap. She also noted that the City is working with the Palos
  Verdes Land Conservancy (PVPLC) with alternative project plans and that the
  PVPLC is assisting with fundraising efforts as well.

  8.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 11, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR PERSICHINA ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:43 PM TO THE NEXT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
March 18, 2025
   PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON APRIL 15, 2025, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD IN THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CITY HALL.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Lou Persichina
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
March 18, 2025
